BV-02 / What it rests on

What does unlimited funding rest on, and what decides the order you build it in?

  • Your personal credit comes first, then each business, and the roadmap built from your own report tells you which move is next.
  • Out of order, every application spends a hard inquiry on a file the bank isn't ready to approve.
  • Kept in order, it builds into five to ten aged companies, each with its own revenue.
  • Here's what's really going on. The goal is funding that keeps coming in, year after year, and I call that UNLIMITED funding.
  • It rests on three things set up right: your personal credit, your businesses, and a clear roadmap from where you are today to where you're going.
  • The ORDER matters most. Your personal credit comes first, then each business, and the roadmap from your own file tells you which move is next.
  • Out of order, every application spends a hard inquiry on a file the bank isn't ready to approve, and that inquiry stays put for the next bank to read.
  • Kept in order, it builds into five to ten aged companies, each with its own revenue, and a bank reads each one by itself.

BV-03 / The code

About 90,000 lines of code build your roadmap, and the six checks start in this block.

  • With the Fundhub engines around it, that grows to about 90,000 lines across 323 files, and the whole app runs close to 580,000.
  • The engine checks your score, your cards used and your negative items first, then your main card, your hard inquiries and how deep your file runs.
  • Your file goes through all six, and the first three decide whether any dollar figure shows up for you.
  • When a company says it has an algorithm, you should get to see it. This is real code, straight from the engine that reads your file.
  • UnderwriteIQ runs on 37,097 lines of code across 145 files. With the Fundhub engines around it, that's about 90,000 lines, and the whole app is close to 580,000.
  • This block lists the engine's six personal checks. On screen are the first three: a score of 700 or higher, cards used at 30 percent or less, and no negative items.
  • The other three are your main card, your hard inquiries, and how deep your file runs. Every check weighs EXACTLY the same.
  • Those first three work as a gate. Pass all three and the engine calls your personal file fundable, and only then does a dollar figure show up at all.

BV-05 / Your businesses

The engine reads every company you add by itself, with five checks of its own.

  • The app keeps each business separate and never adds them together, and the engine's code holds that same rule.
  • In the engine, a company two years old reads at four times the business funding of one under a year old.
  • Your personal file gets ready first. Then business one, then business two.
  • Now the businesses. Every company you add in the app gets read by the engine on its own, with its own five checks.
  • Read the line on the screen. The app keeps each business separate and never adds them together, and the engine's code holds that same rule.
  • Here's why that matters to you. Age counts in the engine, and a company two years old reads at FOUR times the business funding of one under a year old.
  • That's why filing your LLC sits early on the checklist. A company's age counts from the day it's filed with the state, and the filing is your move.
  • Your personal file gets ready first. Then business one, then business two, and you don't need a company at all to get started.
